name: Tomas Usman

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What is a normal workday?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I play guitar behind singers at the local radio station, teach beginners on Saturdays and record extra parts when asked. I have a bachelor’s degree in music and years of sessions, but the station still pays modestly for this town.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What do you enjoy, and what is wearing?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I like finding the right chord under a singer without crowding the voice. A cancelled call wears on me because the mortgage and the children’s activities keep their dates.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the local radio producer that AI sorting interview slots is handy, but the station still calls me to play guitar behind singers. I would keep the Tuesday recording slot and my weekend pupils.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We have only three weeks of expenses saved, though I have played professionally for years and hold a music bachelor’s. My partner’s repair-shop pay changes with the number of cars, so the mortgage still worries me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will keep the Tuesday radio calls and Saturday guitar lessons this winter. I already use AI sometimes to format chord sheets, but I check each change against my guitar before sending it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the household account already. One missed radio call makes the grocery week tight.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happened when a singer cancelled?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last month a singer cancelled and my 70 session fee did not arrive. We delayed the children’s swimming payment until my Saturday lessons cleared.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What can you teach a new guitarist that a sheet cannot?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could teach a young player to follow a singer without crowding the voice. A neat chord sheet cannot listen for a singer’s breath.

I would keep the **Tuesday recording slot** and paid pupils.
think: Our **three-week savings** and variable repair-shop pay leave the mortgage exposed.
One lost **70 session fee** reaches the children’s activities.
do: Keep **Tuesday radio calls** and Saturday guitar lessons this winter.
Check current **AI chord sheets** against my guitar before sending them.
Delay the **children’s swimming payment** after a cancelled radio session until lesson fees clear.
feel: I feel **anxious** because one missed session changes weekly spending.
S0.quote: A neat chord sheet cannot listen for a singer’s breath.
fieldNote: His **experience and music degree** coexist with low local pay and barely three weeks of savings.
The cancelled **70 session** delayed children’s swimming, grounding baseline anxiety.

steps.text: Keep Tuesday radio sessions and Saturday beginner guitar lessons
Delay children’s swimming payment after a cancelled radio session

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the station may use AI to draft jingles, book singers and check parts, so paid guitar sessions need a written schedule. I would ask the producer which calls remain live.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My simple guitar overdubs could lose buyers first, and the station could stretch one session player across more shows. My partner’s repair-shop wage would not cover the mortgage on its own.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next month I would bring three radio invoices to the producer and ask for the next quarter’s paid slots. If calls fall in the first year, I would cut the rented practice booth and ask the youth centre for a paid guitar group only if a staff member supervises, preparation is paid and pickup fits.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious about the station pay, although the producer has not announced a cut. I can ask for a real list before changing the family budget.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you stop renting first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The booth costs 55 each month. I would practise at home if radio calls drop, rather than trim the children’s school transport.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you run the youth group now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have taught pairs, not eight children at once. I would ask a senior tutor to observe a group first if the centre pays for that hour.

say: I would ask for **written radio slots** before the station changes calls.
I would say **live overdubs** still need a clear fee.
think: My **guitar overdubs** could lose buyers as AI drafts music.
Fewer **radio calls** would leave repair-shop pay short of the mortgage.
do: Take three **radio invoices** to the producer next month.
Cancel the **55 practice booth** if radio calls fall.
Ask about **paid youth group** only after funded observation, with staff, preparation pay and pickup fit.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a plausible drop in my own station pay.
S1.quote: My partner’s repair-shop wage would not cover the mortgage on its own.
fieldNote: The radio call risk reaches **mortgage money**, not only optional spending on music.
A youth-centre group needs **paid observation** plus staff, preparation time and pickup fit before he can take eight children.

steps.text: Cancel 55 monthly practice booth if radio calls fall

Keep Saturday guitar pupils while radio slots are checked
Ask centre about paid group only after funded observation, with staff, preparation pay and pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the station that AGI by 2028 could make jingles and parts cheaply, but a singer still needs a guitarist in the room. I would ask for signed live-session dates.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect overdub fees to go in 2028 and the producer may cut the regular Tuesday calls. Robots that play hands-on parts arrive around 2031, but the station can replace a live session with a file before then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Tomorrow I would ask for a signed radio schedule and check whether the youth centre has a posted paid guitar-tutor opening. If 2028 AGI cancels my calls, I would apply only if the job accepts my music degree, pays preparation and fits school pickup; I would call the lender before a missed mortgage payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be alarmed because I expect the overdub income to fall and Tuesday calls could go too. Three weeks in the bank will not cover a slow job search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the youth-centre opening is gone?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep Saturday pupils until a centre offer is signed. If the centre post is already filled, I would ask the radio station for a shorter paid shift rather than tell the family I have a job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What makes a centre offer worth taking?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The centre offer must be written, and the net pay after travel must beat the lost radio calls. My partner can cover pickup twice a week, not every afternoon.

say: I would request **signed radio dates** before the next season.
I would say **live singer support** still merits a fee.
think: My **overdub fees** likely end in 2028 before 2031 playing robots.
The station may also cut **Tuesday sessions** before robots arrive.
do: Ask for a **signed radio schedule** and check posted centre vacancy tomorrow.
Apply for **paid centre tutor post** after 2028 cuts only with degree fit, preparation pay, pickup and better net travel pay.
Call the **mortgage lender** before a missed payment if radio calls end.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by expected fee loss against three weeks saved.
S2.quote: Three weeks in the bank will not cover a slow job search.
fieldNote: He separates **2028 recording loss** from the 2031 robot arrival.
The centre fallback requires **posted paid opening** and degree fit, preparation pay, pickup and written net gain.

steps.text: Apply for posted paid tutor job if 2028 radio calls fall, degree and pickup fit
Call mortgage lender before missing payment if radio calls end
Keep Saturday guitar pupils until centre offer is signed
Accept centre job only if preparation paid and written net pay beats radio fees

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the station that AGI by 2031 gives us years to train another player for live sessions. I would ask the youth centre to pay for a proper group-teaching course, not just hand me eight children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My overdubs probably go by 2031, but I could earn more teaching by then. Robots around 2034 may play guitar parts, though I cannot tell whether the producer would want one beside a singer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This autumn I would ask the youth centre for two paid observations with a senior teacher if the hours fit pickup. If the tutor approves me for eight pupils, I would take a paid group only with another staff member, paid preparation and a written term; in the first year after 2031 I would keep it only while enrollment and childcare hold.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious about the missing overdubs until a real class pays. Five years helps me practise teaching, but the mortgage is monthly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a senior tutor show you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The senior tutor would show me how to keep eight guitars together without shouting. I would not take a large group just because I have a music degree.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How many paid pupils cover the room?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The group needs eight paid places to cover the centre’s room fee. With four, I would keep private lessons and ask for another term, not subsidise empty chairs.

feel: I feel **anxious** until enrolled pupils replace overdub fees.
S3.quote: I would not take a large group just because I have a music degree.
fieldNote: His degree does not replace **paid observation** and tutor approval for eight pupils.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the children that AGI by 2036 gives us a decade to learn another way to earn and still play together. I would keep paid radio work while a producer books it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2036 a paid youth group might replace overdubs if enough pupils return. Robots around 2039 could play a guitar track, but our mortgage will need paying for many winters before then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Starting this year I would save spare Saturday lesson fees after the mortgage and food are paid. In the first year after 2036 I would compare actual radio and teaching pay, and apply for a posted paid centre role only if both shrink and its written net pay after travel and childcare is higher.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would feel anxious because the family still has only three weeks saved. A decade gives me time to build a cushion but does not settle this winter’s bill.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you put money away every month?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Some months there is no extra lesson fee. I would skip saving rather than borrow to fill the account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you teach the children about work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the children to learn a skill, show up prepared and ask what the work pays. The nicest recording in the world cannot clear a mortgage by itself.

S4.quote: The nicest recording in the world cannot clear a mortgage by itself.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because overdubs and Tuesday calls could go before a paid teaching group is ready. Signed radio dates, a suitable posted centre role and lender help before arrears would protect us.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who pays the player who stays after the singer leaves. My guitar is still work when the red studio light goes dark.

headlineQuote: My guitar is still work when the red studio light goes dark.
portrait: At **43**, Tomas is an experienced session guitarist with a music bachelor’s degree, two children, a mortgage and three weeks saved.
His partner’s **variable repair-shop pay** and low local fees make even AI Plateau anxious.
He uses **AI occasionally** for chord sheets and would seek paid observation before a larger youth group.
Across AGI dates he protects **radio and lesson pay**, moving only for posted roles with stronger net income and workable pickup.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could erase overdubs and radio calls before Tomas builds a paid teaching group.
whatWouldHelp: **Signed radio dates**, a suitable paid centre role and early mortgage help would give Tomas a route.
